fichas_metodo.transistor: Individual mean: average net retirement pension in the province (Social Security), over 12 months. It is the mean because Social Security does not publish the median pension by province.
fichas_metodo.peon: Own figure: the net income typed in, for one person or for two with the second income, over 12 months.

mapa.region: Map of Europe of the overburden rate
mapa.titulo_paises: Europe by country; Spain by autonomous community

mapa.nota_regiones: Eurostat publishes the rate by NUTS 2 region only for the whole population. Where it does not, the country or NUTS 1 figure is shown, hatched. Some countries have no regional figure in some years (Denmark, until 2024), and Eurostat sometimes publishes two regions together (FI19_20): they are left blank.
mapa.nota_paises: By tenure or age, Eurostat publishes countries. Spain is shown by autonomous community from INE microdata with three pooled waves ({desde}–{hasta}), because a single wave does not give a large enough sample: countries and communities do not cover the same period.

escalera.subtitulo: Rank among {n} areas and references, highest first · {periodo}

serie.subtitulo: Whole population and market-rate tenants, compared with the EU-27
serie.fuente: Eurostat (ilc_lvho07a, ilc_lvho07c), from the first year published: for Spain, the whole population since 2004 and market-rate renting since 2007; the EU-27, since 2010. From 2023 to 2025, the calculation from EU-SILC microdata reproduces these figures (±0.1 points).
serie.rupturas: Break in series (Eurostat flag «b»; hollow point and broken line): {lista}. Figures before and after are not fully comparable.
serie.rupturas_atlas: Break in series set by the atlas, not flagged by Eurostat (hollow point and broken line): {lista}. Since the 2013 survey, INE has obtained income by combining the interview with administrative records (tax agency, Social Security and the foral treasuries), and income is the denominator of the rate.
serie.ruptura_atlas: break in series set by the atlas (income from administrative records since 2013), not flagged by Eurostat
serie.grafico: Overburden rate in Spain and the EU-27, whole population and market-rate renting, {desde}–{hasta}

desgloses.titulo: Spain by tenure, age and income
desgloses.subtitulo: EU-SILC microdata, own calculation · each figure with its sample
desgloses.nota: The under-18 and 15-to-29 groups overlap. «Owner» and «Tenant or rent-free» combine Eurostat’s categories.
desgloses.nota_quintil: Quintiles of equivalised disposable income (household income divided by its consumption units, modified OECD scale) of the whole population, weighted by person. Spain only: no quintile by country or by autonomous community.

comunidades.titulo: Communities on the map: figure and sample

metodo.hipoteca: Only mortgage interest counts, not capital repayments.
metodo.renta: Income refers to the year before the survey: the 2025 survey records 2024 incomes.
metodo.muestra: No confidence intervals: the public microdata do not include the sample design. Each INE figure carries its number of observations and the EU-SILC reliability flag: not published below 20; hatched from 20 to 49.
metodo.compuerta: The calculation reproduces Eurostat’s figures for Spain, each autonomous community, market-rate tenants and each age group (±0.1 points).
metodo.marcas: Eurostat figures carry their flags next to the value: b, break in series; u, low reliability (hatched on the map); e, estimate; p, provisional.

acceso.definicion: People aged 16 or over who actively looked for housing in the last 12 months without moving. Overburden misses them: it measures those already housed.
acceso.razon: Main reason: excessive price, for {x}% of those who searched without success.
acceso.fuente: INE, EU-SILC {anio}, module on difficulties in accessing housing (published tables).

razones.vivienda: The dwelling did not meet the requirements
razones.condiciones: The conditions to rent or buy were not met

otras_cifras.titulo: Why it differs from other figures
otras_cifras.metodo: Other calculations add the whole mortgage payment or count households instead of people: they answer a different question.
otras_cifras.total: Outright owners dominate the total; the burden is concentrated among market-rate tenants.

pie.fuentes: Sources: INE, Living Conditions Survey (EU-SILC microdata and housing access module); Eurostat (ilc_lvho07a, ilc_lvho07c and ilc_lvho07_r).
pie.licencia: Data and texts: CC BY-SA 4.0. Map boundaries: © EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries (GISCO, non-commercial use).

historico.titulo_pagina: Time machine · De renta en renta
historico.descripcion: Spanish series since 1987: years of income and burden of buying a home, mortgage interest rates, appraised value, average wage and housing as a problem (CIS)
historico.entradilla: How many years of income a home cost, what share of income the first-year mortgage payments took, at what interest rate, what a square metre was appraised at and what an employee earned on average, period by period. Series from the Banco de España, the Ministry of Housing (MIVAU) and INE on the same time axis; the appraised value, also by region. At the end, housing as a problem in the CIS barometers, since 2014.

hist-renta.titulo: Years of income to buy a home
hist-renta.subtitulo: Average price of a standard open-market home divided by the gross annual income of the median household. Quarterly.
hist-renta.fuente: Source: own elaboration with data extracted from the Banco de España website (www.bde.es): Summary indicators, table 1.5, series D_TKB57110_IPV. Data downloaded on {version}.

hist-esfuerzo.subtitulo: First-year payments on a loan for 80% of the value of the standard home, as a percentage of the disposable income of the median household, without tax deductions. Quarterly. This is not the map's «Mortgage payment over household income» (indicator 17): same calculation, but with an 80 m² flat and the average net income of all households, which is higher than the median household's, so it comes out at about half (Spain, 2024: 18.1% on the map; 34.6% on average here).
hist-esfuerzo.fuente: Source: own elaboration with data extracted from the Banco de España website (www.bde.es): Summary indicators, table 1.5, series D_TKB57210_IPV. Data downloaded on {version}.

hist-tipos.subtitulo: Rate on new loans for house purchase, the same one used to compute the theoretical burden; as a reference, the one-year MIBOR up to 1998 and the 12-month Euribor since 1999, which are different indices. In percent. Monthly.
hist-tipos.fuente: Source: own elaboration with data extracted from the Banco de España website (www.bde.es): Summary indicators, table 1.5, series D_IMVTIPLV; Statistical Bulletin, table 19.1, series D_1E723706.EUR (up to 1998) and D_1NBAF472 (since 1999). Data downloaded on {version}.

hist-tasado.subtitulo: Average appraisal value per square metre, not the price paid. Quarterly, since 1995; Spain and each region.
hist-tasado.fuente: Source: MIVAU, Appraised value of open-market housing (online statistical bulletin, table 35101000). Data downloaded on {version}.

hist-sueldo.subtitulo: Gross wages and salaries of the whole economy divided by the employees of the year. Annual; the series starts in 1995. It lies above the AEAT average wage.
hist-sueldo.fuente: Source: INE, Annual Spanish National Accounts, base 2020 (tables 71129 and 71133). Data downloaded on {version}.

series.tipo_hipotecas: Average rate on mortgage loans over three years
series.mibor_euribor: Reference: one-year MIBOR up to 1998 and 12-month Euribor since 1999 (different indices)

euros.nota_constantes_anual: In {anio} euros, adjusted for inflation: each year multiplied by the general CPI of {anio} and divided by that of its year (INE, annual averages of the general index, base 2025).
euros.nota_antes: From {desde} to {hasta} INE has no index in base 2025: in {anio} euros the series starts in {primero}, and those years are shown only in euros of each year.

euros.nota_corrientes: In euros of each year, not adjusted for inflation.

historico.grafico: Chart of {serie}, from {desde} to {hasta}. With the chart selected, the arrow keys step through the periods.
historico.cis_subtitulo: Share of respondents who name housing among Spain’s three main problems and among the three that affect them most personally, with spontaneous answers. Monthly, since 2014; no barometer in August.
historico.cis_huecos: Months without a figure, where the line breaks: {n}.
historico.cis_aviso: Opinion, not a register: the series measures how many people name housing as a problem, not its price or what it costs to pay for it.
historico.cis_fuente: Source: own elaboration with data from the Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS, www.cis.es), monthly barometers, under a CC BY 4.0 licence. Changes: figures rounded to one decimal; the six months published only as PDF (July 2014 and five in 2025), transcribed by hand. The CIS neither takes part in nor sponsors this atlas.
historico.cis_sin_datos: There are no CIS data in this copy of the website (datos/cis_vivienda.json). They are generated with targets::tar_make(names = ficheros_web_cis).
historico.cis_metodo: Housing as a problem (CIS): in the monthly barometer, share of respondents who name housing, without a list of answers, among Spain’s three main problems or among the three that affect them most personally. It is an opinion survey, not a register. Since January 2014; no barometer in August. The months whose results are only in PDF (July 2014 and February, April, May, June and July 2025) are transcribed by hand, with the link to each PDF and its check. Validation: the series reproduces the figures the CIS gives in its press releases.

metodo.renta: Years of income (Banco de España): average price of a standard open-market home (93.75 m² until 2004; afterwards, the average floor area of registered sales) divided by the estimated gross annual income of the median household, based on the Survey of Household Finances, the National Accounts and the Labour Force Survey.
metodo.esfuerzo: Theoretical burden (Banco de España): first-year payments on a loan for 80% of the value of that home, at the average rate on new housing loans and the average mortgage term, as a percentage of the disposable income of the median household. No tax deductions throughout the series.
metodo.tipos: Rates (Banco de España): the main line is the rate on new loans to households for house purchase, since January 1989, the same one the Banco de España uses for the theoretical burden (up to 2002, under its Circular 8/1990; since 2003, under Circular 4/2002: break marked). As a reference, the one-year MIBOR up to December 1998 and the 12-month Euribor since January 1999: they are different indices and the change is marked.
metodo.tasado: Appraised value (MIVAU): average appraisal value of open-market housing per square metre, not the price paid. A year in the Banco de España table is the simple mean of its four quarters.
metodo.sueldo: Wage (INE, National Accounts): gross wages and salaries of the whole economy divided by the employees of each year, including those who work part of the year or part-time. The series starts in 1995, with the current accounting base. It lies above the AEAT average wage used by the «Young adult, 26 to 35» token (in 2024, €31,200 against €24,962): the National Accounts divide by the average number of employees over the year, so someone who works a few months counts only for that share, and they include the Basque Country and Navarre, which the AEAT does not cover.
metodo.euros: Euros: the appraised value and the average wage open in euros of the last year with an annual CPI average, adjusted for inflation: each period is multiplied by the general CPI of that year and divided by that of its own year (INE, annual averages of the general index, base 2025; a quarter uses the average of its year). INE does not provide that index before 2002, so in constant euros both series start in 2002; periods of the current year, with no annual average yet, are left out as well. «Euros of each year» shows the figures as the source publishes them, from 1995. The other series are ratios or interest rates and do not change. The map, its legends, the stories and the data table are always in euros of each year.
metodo.mezcla: Each series keeps its source, unit and period (quarter, month or year): they are not combined into an indicator. The charts share the time axis so that they can be read one below the other.
metodo.compuerta: Validation: the series reproduce the figures the Banco de España publishes in its PDF table and the reference rate published in the Official State Gazette; the MIVAU appraised value matches the one reproduced by the Banco de España in every quarter since 1995. If the Banco de España revises a series, the gate warns and asks for the reference to be updated, without blocking.

pie.fuentes: Sources: Banco de España (Summary indicators, table 1.5; Statistical Bulletin, table 19.1), MIVAU (Appraised value of open-market housing), INE (Annual Spanish National Accounts) and CIS (monthly barometers).
pie.bde: Source of the Banco de España series: own elaboration with data extracted from the Banco de España website (www.bde.es). The Banco de España neither takes part in nor sponsors this atlas.

renta_persona.definicion: Average disposable income of residents: total income net of taxes and contributions of all households in the tract, divided by its population.
renta_persona.calculo: Published by INE (ADRH) from tax records. Years published on another tract map are carried to the 2021 tracts as a population-weighted mean; where a tract has to be split, the status becomes «estimated».
renta_persona.lectura: Income for year t with population on 1 January of t + 1. Excludes imputed rent of owner-occupied housing. Published about 22 months after the reference year.

renta_hogar.definicion: Average disposable income of households in the tract.
renta_hogar.calculo: Published by INE (ADRH). On other tract maps, mean weighted by the number of households (population divided by average household size), with the same status rules as indicator 1.
renta_hogar.lectura: This is household income, often with several earners, not a wage. It is the denominator of median rent over the area's average household income (14) and the income of the «neighbourhood household» token.

renta_uc_mediana.definicion: Median disposable income per consumption unit (modified OECD scale): half of the tract population lives in households with lower equivalised income and half with higher.
renta_uc_mediana.calculo: Published by INE (ADRH) at each scale; medians are not aggregated. On other tract maps the value of a single source tract is copied (the same tract or one contributing at least 95% of street numbers); if none dominates, it is left blank.
renta_uc_mediana.lectura: Comparable across household sizes. It underlies the relative poverty thresholds (indicator 5).

peso_salarios.definicion: Share of the gross income of the tract's residents that comes from wages.
peso_salarios.calculo: Published by INE (ADRH, income by source: wages, pensions, unemployment benefits, other benefits and other income, adding up to 100). Years published on another tract map are carried to the 2021 tracts as a mean weighted by each tract's gross income (average gross income per person × population); where a tract has to be split, the status becomes «estimated». Municipalities, provinces, regions and Spain use the published figure.
peso_salarios.lectura: Links neighbourhood income to wages: a low share means income depends more on pensions, benefits or other income. No data for Álava until 2019, Gipuzkoa in 2015 or most of Navarre until 2020.

bajo_60_mediana.nombre: Population below 60% of median income per consumption unit
bajo_60_mediana.definicion: Population with income per consumption unit below 60% of the Spanish median (until 2022, the median of the common tax territory, without the Basque Country and Navarre).
bajo_60_mediana.calculo: Published by INE (ADRH, relative thresholds, both sexes). Years published on another tract map are carried to the 2021 tracts as a population-weighted mean, since the threshold is the same across Spain each year; where a tract has to be split, the status becomes «estimated». Municipalities, provinces, regions and Spain use the published figure.
bajo_60_mediana.lectura: National threshold, not regional: the same income counts the same everywhere, although living costs differ. Break in 2023: the threshold moves from the median of the common tax territory to that of all of Spain. No data for Álava until 2019, Gipuzkoa in 2015 or Navarre until 2020.

gini.definicion: Gini index of income per consumption unit in the tract: 0 if everyone has the same income, 100 if one person holds all of it.
gini.calculo: Published by INE (ADRH), which first replaces the lowest 1.5% and the highest 1.5% of incomes with the nearest value. On other tract maps the value of a single source tract is copied (the same tract or one contributing at least 95% of street numbers); if none dominates, it is left blank. Municipalities, provinces, regions and Spain use the published figure.
gini.lectura: Measures inequality within the neighbourhood, not between neighbourhoods. No data for Álava until 2019, Gipuzkoa in 2015 or Navarre until 2020.

salario_medio.nombre: Average annual wage per employee (total and aged 26 to 35)
salario_medio.definicion: Average gross annual wage of employees with tax residence in the province, overall and aged 26 to 35.
salario_medio.calculo: Published by the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT, Labour market and pensions in tax sources, table by province, age and sex): wages / employees, overall and for the 26 to 35 age band; regions and Spain, with their published figure. The Basque Country and Navarre are not covered (foral tax residence) and have no data.
salario_medio.lectura: Actual pay over the year: it includes people who worked only a few months. It is a mean, not a median; the «young adult, 26 to 35» token converts it to a median with the median-to-mean ratio of the estimated average wage in its region, and then to monthly net pay spread over 12, with the employee's social security contribution and the average AEAT withholding by region and income band (plan §3.1, method B).

alquiler_mes.definicion: Median monthly rent of current main-residence tenancies in the tract, by building type (apartment and single-family); the first and third quartiles are also published.
alquiler_mes.calculo: Published by the Housing Ministry (SERPAVI) from rents declared in personal income tax and the Cadastre, on the 2021 tracts for the whole series. Not published with fewer than 10 tenancies.
alquiler_mes.lectura: Covers the whole rented stock, not new contracts: newcomers pay more. It only counts landlords who are natural persons and declare the letting as a main residence in personal income tax: companies and public housing, undeclared lettings and lettings to relatives are left out (Housing Ministry methodology, 18-Mar-2026). The Basque Country and Navarre join SERPAVI between 2021 and 2024.

alquiler_m2.definicion: Median monthly rent per square metre of current main-residence tenancies in the tract, by building type (apartment and single-family).
alquiler_m2.calculo: Published by the Housing Ministry (SERPAVI), using Cadastre floor area.
alquiler_m2.lectura: Allows comparing tracts with different dwelling sizes and underlies the pay needed (21). Same universe as 8: only landlords who are natural persons declaring the letting in personal income tax.

var_alquiler.definicion: Annual change in the Rental Housing Price Index.
var_alquiler.calculo: Published by INE (IPVA), which follows the same tenancies and separates new from existing contracts.
var_alquiler.lectura: An index, not a price level: it shows trends, not how much is paid.

precio_compra_m2.definicion: Average price per square metre of housing sales entered in the land registries.
precio_compra_m2.calculo: Published by the Spanish Land Registrars' Association (Real Estate Registry Statistics, open data under the ODbL): average price per m² of housing for the year, that of the fourth quarter, which accumulates the calendar year; province, region and Spain, each with its published figure.
precio_compra_m2.lectura: A registered sale price, not an asking price or an appraisal. It is not compared with the Notaries' price per m², which measures a different floor area; the province is the finest level.

valor_tasado_m2.definicion: Average appraised value per square metre of open-market housing.
valor_tasado_m2.calculo: Quarterly figure published by the Housing Ministry from mortgage appraisals; the year is the average of its four quarters weighted by the number of appraisals.
valor_tasado_m2.lectura: An appraisal value, not a price paid; only municipalities above 25,000 inhabitants.

precio_oferta.unidad: € per m² (rent: per m² per month)
precio_oferta.definicion: Average price per square metre in rental and sale listings.
precio_oferta.calculo: Monthly figure from each portal’s aggregated press-room reports (Idealista: the author’s extraction, matched to INE codes in inventario/portales_idealista_territorios.csv; format in R/fuente_portales.R); never individual listings. One value per year, portal and transaction: the mean of the published months, with at least 9 (with fewer, no data), or the annual figure if the portal publishes one; at each level, the one the portal publishes for that level. The last month of the year is no longer used (10 Nov 2026). A removable layer (PORTALES=FALSE by default), web only: not in the long table or the downloads.
precio_oferta.lectura: An asking price, private asking-price data: not combined with contracts, deeds or appraisals, nor one portal with another.

esfuerzo_residentes.nombre: Median rent over the area's average household income
esfuerzo_residentes.definicion: Share of the annual income of the average household in the tract, across all its households (owners included), that the median rent of that same tract would take.
esfuerzo_residentes.calculo: Median monthly rent of flats × 12 / average net household income, same year, × 100. Census tract and municipality. If either term is confidential or missing, so is the result.
esfuerzo_residentes.lectura: It is not renters' burden: it divides the rent of current tenancies by the average income of all households in the tract, owners included, and barely tells areas apart (in 2024, a median of 18.3% in the fifth of tracts with the lowest household income and 17.5% in the highest). Expensive areas look affordable because higher-income people live there.

peso_alquiler_ingreso.definicion: Share of a token’s net monthly income (minimum wage, young adult, pensioner or the user’s own pay) that 50 m² of rent in the tract would take.
peso_alquiler_ingreso.calculo: Median rent per m² of flats × 50 / token’s net monthly income spread over 12 payments, × 100. Computed in the browser for the chosen token, with the token’s income from the same year as the rent (each year’s minimum wage, young-adult pay and pension, 2015 to 2024); if the token lacks that year, the latest is used and this is stated.
peso_alquiler_ingreso.lectura: Measures what the rent of current tenancies in the tract (those already renting) would take from a given income; it is not the price of moving in today, which asking rents measure. Read by bands (up to 30%, 30–40% and over 40%), not as an exact figure.

anios_salario_compra.nombre: Years of wages to buy a home
anios_salario_compra.definicion: Years of reference gross pay needed to buy a standard dwelling.
anios_salario_compra.calculo: Appraised value per m² × standard floor area (80 m² by default) / average gross annual wage per employee (Tax Agency), same year; for a municipality, the wage of its province.
anios_salario_compra.lectura: Uses the appraised value, not the deed price, and ignores financing and down payment; see mortgage payment over household income (17). No data for the Basque Country and Navarre, which lack Tax Agency wages.

esfuerzo_hipotecario.definicion: Share of the average net income of the area's households taken by the first-year payment of a mortgage on an 80 m² flat.
esfuerzo_hipotecario.calculo: First-year annual payment of a French-amortisation loan for 80% of the appraised value of 80 m², over 25 years at the Bank of Spain's rate on new home-purchase loans (average of the year's twelve months), divided by the average net household income from the ADRH (INE) for the same year and area, × 100. The income is the one published at each level; where INE does not publish it, no value for the province and the region (Navarre until 2020, Álava and the Basque Country until 2019, Gipuzkoa in 2015) and, for Spain until 2020, the household-weighted mean of the municipalities, estimated.
esfuerzo_hipotecario.lectura: A theoretical calculation: it assumes the remaining 20% and purchase costs are available. It is not the Banco de España's «theoretical first-year burden» shown in the Time machine: the calculation is the same, but the Banco de España uses the standard home it defines and the income of the median household, while here it is an 80 m² flat and the average net income of all households in the area, which is higher. That is why this figure comes out at about half (Spain, 2024: 18.1% here and 34.6% on average for the Banco de España).

hogares_alquiler.definicion: Households renting as a share of all households (main residences) in the tract.
hogares_alquiler.calculo: From INE’s 2021 and 2011 Population and Housing Censuses, on the 2021 tracts; 2011 is carried from the 2011 Census tracts with its conversion table.
hogares_alquiler.lectura: A snapshot at two dates, not an annual series. The 2011 Census is sample-based: its tract figures are estimates.

viviendas_turisticas.nombre: Tourist dwellings as a share of all dwellings
viviendas_turisticas.definicion: Tourist dwellings as a share of all dwellings in the tract.
viviendas_turisticas.calculo: Tourist dwellings from INE’s experimental statistics (platform listings) over all dwellings in the Census, the denominator used by INE: the 2011 Census up to February 2023 and the 2021 Census from August 2023. From August 2020 to February 2023 on the 2011 Census tracts, and from February 2024 on the 2024 tracts, carried to the 2021 tracts with their conversion tables; twice a year.
viviendas_turisticas.lectura: Measures pressure from tourist use. Numerator and denominator are not from the same year: dwellings are those of the 2011 Census up to February 2023 and of the 2021 Census from February 2024. Reference months changed in 2024 (from February and August to May and November).

zona_tensionada.unidad: category (2 whole municipality, 1 part of it, 0 none)
zona_tensionada.definicion: Municipality or area declared a stressed residential market zone under Law 12/2023, in force on 31 December of each year.
zona_tensionada.calculo: Quarterly Housing Ministry resolutions in the BOE listing the zones declared by the autonomous communities (art. 18.2.d): in force for three years from the day after publication. 2 if the declaration covers the whole municipality; 1 if it covers part of it (villages, neighbourhoods or districts), painted on the whole municipality with its own category; 0 with no declaration in force.
zona_tensionada.lectura: A public policy layer, not a market measure: it shows where the measures of Law 12/2023 apply (caps on new-contract rents and a local definition of large landlord), not how much housing costs.

sueldo_necesario.nombre: Net monthly pay needed to stay under the threshold
sueldo_necesario.definicion: Net monthly pay needed so that the tract's median monthly rent does not exceed 30% of pay. Alongside, the theoretical minimum: the same calculation for a 50 m² flat.
sueldo_necesario.calculo: Median monthly rent of flats / 0.30 (threshold can be changed to 40%). Theoretical minimum (cut superficie, group 50): median rent per m² of flats × 50 / 0.30 (floor area can be changed to 70 or 90 m² on the website). Each figure carries the status of its rent.
sueldo_necesario.lectura: It is rent expressed in another unit, not a new indicator. The main figure pays for the tract's median rented home, around 79 m² at the median; the 50 m² minimum falls below it and is never given without it. The 30% is a convention and counts rent only: Law 12/2023 and Eurostat also count utilities and use household income. On the website, renters' other housing costs (ECV) can be added.

sobrecarga.definicion: People living in households whose total housing costs, net of housing allowances, exceed 40% of disposable income, also net of allowances.
sobrecarga.calculo: EU-SILC microdata (INE) with Eurostat’s method: only mortgage interest counts; previous-year income; person weights. Reproduces Eurostat figures (±0.1 points). Region × tenure and age breakdowns pool three waves.
sobrecarga.lectura: Measures the burden on those already housed; outright owners dominate it and it misses people unable to leave home. Read it alongside unsuccessful housing search (23) and by tenure, especially market-rate renting.

busqueda_sin_exito.definicion: People aged 16 and over who actively looked for housing in the last 12 months without moving.
busqueda_sin_exito.calculo: Published by INE in the tables of the 2025 EU-SILC module on housing access difficulties, with the main reason (mostly price).
busqueda_sin_exito.lectura: A one-off measure (2025). It captures those trying to move in and failing, unlike the overburden rate.

contratos_alquiler.definicion: Number of current main-residence tenancies from which SERPAVI computes the area's median rent, by building type (apartment and single-family).
contratos_alquiler.calculo: Count published by the Housing Ministry (SERPAVI). With fewer than 10 tenancies the median is not published; 0 means there are no registered rental contracts, which is not the same as «no data».
contratos_alquiler.lectura: Shows how many tenancies support the median: with fewer than 30, the tract profile flags «few contracts». It accompanies 8, 9, 14, 15 and 21 and has no map of its own.

margen_alquiler_mes.nombre: Approximate margin of the median monthly rent
margen_alquiler_mes.definicion: Approximate standard error of the median monthly rent (8), as a percentage of the median, by building type.
margen_alquiler_mes.calculo: 0.929 × (P75 − P25) / (P50 × √n), using the SERPAVI quartiles and tenancies (n); only where the median is published (10 or more tenancies).
margen_alquiler_mes.lectura: Order of magnitude of the noise in the median: it assumes a regular distribution within the area and does not correct for current rather than new tenancies. It accompanies 8, 14 and the main figure of 21, which are monthly rent in another unit.

margen_alquiler_m2.nombre: Approximate margin of the median rent per m²
margen_alquiler_m2.definicion: Approximate standard error of the median rent per square metre (9), as a percentage of the median, by building type.
margen_alquiler_m2.calculo: 0.929 × (P75 − P25) / (P50 × √n), using the SERPAVI rent-per-m² quartiles and tenancies (n); only where the median is published (10 or more tenancies).
margen_alquiler_m2.lectura: It also applies to 15 and to the 50 m² minimum of 21, which are rent per m² in another unit: the profile warns when «Can you make rent?» sits on the edge between two bands.

fuentes.mivau_serpavi: State Rental Price Reference System (SERPAVI): database
fuentes.registradores: Land Registry Real Estate Statistics: residential property sales by province (Spanish Land Registrars' Association; database under the ODbL)
fuentes.mivau_transacciones: Real estate transactions (sales): average value of open-market housing sales
fuentes.ine_hipotecas: Mortgage Statistics (H): average initial interest rate
fuentes.portales: Asking-price reports (Idealista and Fotocasa press rooms)
fuentes.aeat_mercado_trabajo: Labour market and pensions in tax sources
fuentes.boe_smi: Royal Decree on the minimum wage
fuentes.zonas_tensionadas: Declarations of stressed residential market zones
fuentes.ign_au: IGN administrative units (BDDAE): condominiums and territories outside any province
fuentes.ine_callejero: Electoral census street directory (street segments by tract)
fuentes.ine_padron_sc: Population by census tract (annual population census; municipal register)
fuentes.ine_ecv_modulo: Living Conditions Survey 2025: housing access difficulties module (tables)
fuentes.eurostat_ilc_lvho07: Housing cost overburden rate (ilc_lvho07a, ilc_lvho07b, ilc_lvho07c)
fuentes.eurostat_ilc_lvho07_r: Housing cost overburden rate by NUTS 2 region (ilc_lvho07_r)
fuentes.eustat_nastat: Income indicators for the Basque Country (Eustat) and Navarre (Nastat)
fuentes.ine_epa_deciles: Wage deciles of the main job (Labour Force Survey)
fuentes.bde_accesibilidad: Housing affordability indicators (years of income, theoretical burden)
fuentes.calculo_propio: Own calculation from the sources of each term
fuentes.bde_tipos_referencia: Official mortgage market reference interest rates
fuentes.ine_cne: Annual Spanish National Accounts: aggregates by industry (base 2020)
fuentes.cis_barometros: CIS monthly barometers: housing among the main problems
fuentes.ine_ipc: Consumer Price Index (CPI): annual averages of the general index (base 2025)

contrato.nuevo: New contract (signed in the reference year)
contrato.existente: Existing contract (signed before the reference year)

corte.oferta_privada: Private asking-price data: transaction and portal (removable layer, only with PORTALES=TRUE)
corte.superficie: Assumed floor area (theoretical minimum of the pay needed)

estado.estimado: Estimated: the tract boundaries changed and values had to be split

fiabilidad.baja: Small sample (20 to 49 observations): read with caution

tenencia.OWN_NL: Owner with no outstanding mortgage or housing loan
tenencia.RENT_FR: Tenant at reduced price or rent-free

tipologia_p25.VC: Flat in a multi-dwelling building, first quartile
tipologia_p25.VU: Single-family or rural dwelling, first quartile

tipologia_p75.VC: Flat in a multi-dwelling building, third quartile
tipologia_p75.VU: Single-family or rural dwelling, third quartile
